notes:
Added
- Clip Review: go through an episode's clips with the keyboard. Play and scrub each clip right in the app, see why it was picked, move its start and end ([ and ]), fix caption words, and edit the title, description and hashtags with live counters. A safe-zone guide (S) shows where YouTube's buttons sit. Every change makes the clip again, while the previous version keeps playing until the new one is ready. Undo and redo cover the last 50 changes.
- Approve before anything is published: press A to see where the clip goes, when and how (channel, time slot, visibility), then Enter to approve. Changing a clip afterwards takes the approval back, and an upload checks that the clip is still exactly the one you approved.
- Publish kit: export an episode's approved clips into one folder, numbered and named with your style's file-name template, with a text file of titles, descriptions, tags and suggested posting times, ready to drag into YouTube Studio. Copy buttons, "Open YouTube Studio" and "Mark scheduled" help with each clip, and a short guide sets up YouTube Studio's upload defaults once.
- Suggested posting times from your posting times (set them in the Style Studio's brand kit) and daily limit, shown in your time zone and in UTC, including around daylight-saving changes.
- The Style Studio: eight ready-made looks (Hype, Clean, Meme, Cinematic, Minimal, Neon, Comic and Anime Pop) that you can copy and change: caption font, size, colours, outline, a box behind the spoken word, animations, the hook card, the layout and background, output quality, and title, description, hashtag and file-name templates that fill in each new clip. A preview picture updates as you change things.
- Your watermark, burned into every clip: text, your logo or both, in any language (Japanese channel names included), with fills such as gradient, metallic, holographic, neon or your own texture, gentle animations, and a slight change per clip that makes it harder to remove. It stays clear of the platform's buttons.
- A brand kit with your channel's name, logos, colours, fonts and default looks, which you can export to a file and import on your partner's PC.
- Fourteen caption fonts come with Kirinuki now, including Montserrat, Inter, Bebas Neue, Sora and the Japanese-friendly Dela Gothic One and Zen Maru Gothic. You can also add your own fonts and logos; each file is checked carefully before Kirinuki uses it.
- A glossary of character names per series, so names are spelled right and never split across caption lines, and optional masking of swear words in captions.
- Keyboard shortcuts you can change in Settings → Shortcuts.
- The setup guide's test clip can be reviewed and restyled too, so you can try Clip Review, the Publish kit and the Style Studio before importing an episode.
- Every error message now says what happened and what to do, with a "Copy diagnostic report" button that shows you the report first and never includes keys, sign-ins or file paths.
- The licence list in About now includes the new fonts, the swear-word lists (by Shutterstock, CC BY 4.0), Pillow and the OpenType Sanitizer.
